note: Author (UniProt O43464) numbering throughout; PDZ = 359-458. Mobile = the regions the 2024 paper names for apo isolated-PDZ CPMG: 'the amino-terminus, the alpha5 helix and the adjacent loop connecting to beta15, as well as alpha7 and its preceding loop' (HTPDZ-r1 / Fig. 2a-b) and at 283 K 'the beta17-beta18 loop' (HTPDZ-r2). Residue limits from the 5M3N helix/strand records: alpha5 370-381, beta15 391-396, alpha6 400-406, beta16 412-416, alpha7 423-434, beta17 437-443, beta18 446-452; so mobile = 353-362 (N-terminus incl. beta13 359-361), 370-389 (alpha5 + alpha5-beta15 loop), 417-435 (loop + alpha7), 444-446 (beta17-beta18 turn). Core = beta14 364-368, beta15 + loop 390-399, alpha6/beta16 408-416, beta17 436-443, beta18 447-453. 'open' = 2PZD chain A, the only isolated-PDZ crystal (peptide WTMFWV fused to the chain, bound in the groove; HTPDZ-J21); 'closed' = 5M3N chain A, wild-type full-length trimer with the PDZ packed on the protease domain (resting state; HTPDZ-J22 names 1LCY/5FHT as the same closed arrangement). The CPMG minor state is not identified structurally (HTPDZ-r3), so this axis tests only whether any PDZ copy departs from the closed-trimer geometry within the domain. Renumbering: 1LCY, 5FHT and 5WYN are numbered from the mature N-terminus (auth + 133 = UniProt; alignment to 5M3N gives delta 133 over 9-325 with <=4 mismatches, all at the deposited mutations). 7VGE and 8AUK are PDZ-deleted constructs (auth 140-342 only) and 8E2K chains Y/Z lack the PDZ, so those chains carry no mobile residues and get no closure. 2PZD is classed 'apo' by the tool because the peptide is part of the polymer chain; it is peptide-bound.
